items.stem: What best distinguishes a forecast from a budget?

options.text: A forecast is an updated expectation of what will happen; a budget is an agreed plan and target
options.rationale: Correct: forecasts update with reality, budgets are the agreed plan.

options.text: A forecast is always lower than a budget
options.rationale: Direction is not what defines the difference.

options.text: A budget covers one month and a forecast covers one week
options.rationale: Period length does not define them.

items.explanation: Correct: forecasts update with reality, budgets are the agreed plan.

items.stem: Which TWO are features of zero-based budgeting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Every cost must be justified from a zero base each cycle
options.rationale: Correct: nothing is assumed from prior spend.

options.text: It can surface and challenge legacy spending
options.rationale: Correct: a key benefit is exposing embedded costs.

options.text: It simply adds a fixed percentage to last year
It removes the need for any assumptions

items.explanation: Correct: nothing is assumed from prior spend.
